question: Which of two treatments works better, compared within each person?

steps.title: Randomise the order
steps.text: Chance decides the order in which each person gets the treatments: A then B, or B then A. Everyone gets both.

quotes.text: each individual in a crossover trial receives multiple interventions but in a random order; that is, participants are randomised to sequences of interventions.
quotes.where: Methodological features of randomised crossover trials

quotes.text: The allocation might be to sequence one, in which participants have A followed by B, or to sequence two, in which participants have B followed by A.

steps.title: First period
steps.text: Each person takes their first treatment for a set time, and the outcome is measured at the end of it.

quotes.text: Period: a length of time when one treatment was received.

steps.title: Washout
steps.text: A gap with no treatment lets the first one wear off, so it does not leak into the second period.

quotes.text: Washout: a length of time between treatment periods when no treatment is received to allow the treatment to wear off.

steps.title: Swap
steps.text: Each person now gets the other treatment, for the same length of time, measured the same way.

quotes.text: crossover trials provide each participant with two or more sequential treatments in a random order usually separated by a washout period

steps.title: Compare within
steps.text: Compare each person's result on A with their own result on B. Differences between people drop out, which is why far fewer people are needed.

quotes.text: Within a trial, each participant is able to act as his or her own control and permits between and within group comparisons
The analysis of a crossover trial should respect the within participant nature of the comparisons.

carryover.text: the effect of the first intervention persists into the second period so that the observed difference between the treatments depends on the order in which they were received
carryover.where: Methodological features of randomised crossover trials

attrition.text: Patients may drop out after the first intervention period and thus not receive a second or third treatment. This makes within-subject comparison impossible
